defects: The paired roof wings obscure the boiler and reduce workshop readability at settlement distance.
incumbent_comparison: Best-so-far workshop-v002 is technically valid, but its run-004 three-quarter view hides the boiler. v004 under the same current renderer/camera settings opens a center slot and exposes the boiler, stack, gauge, and workbench while retaining roof coverage at the sides.
likely_causes: The wings span too far across the centerline above the existing boiler and stack.
next_action_hypothesis: Keep the workshop footprint, machinery, and outer-bay cover; pull both roof wings outward and narrow them so the boiler and stack remain visible from the same three-quarter settlement camera.

observations.art_direction_fit: Timber, iron, copper, and warm glazing fit the miniature steampunk target, though the closed-over machinery weakens the intended working-workshop read.
observations.close_up_quality: The boiler fittings and gear are visible in close view, but the chosen cover geometry masks much of the focal assembly in the production three-quarter view.
observations.gameplay_readability: The room-scale/settlement-scale captures preserve the open-front access and do not show render geometry blocking the nearby activity area.
observations.geometric_detail: Run-004 close and reverse views show board courses, standing seams, boiler hoops, pipework, a gauge, door straps, and a flywheel, but several important pieces are occluded from the settlement angle.
observations.material_realism: The close capture separates dark iron, copper, timber, and amber glazing with distinct roughness/reflectance; broad roof and wall faces still look smooth at this distance.
observations.proportion: The recorded bounds are within the 26 x 20 x 20 inch brief envelope, and the structure sits at the intended settlement site in the production render.
observations.scale_fidelity: The technical report measures a 26 x 19.94 x 20 inch asset; the candidate is rendered at the existing 0.6 presentation scale beside citizens.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The production three-quarter capture identifies a workshop from its boiler stack, timber frame, glazed opening, and workbench, but two broad roof wings hide most of the boiler and work face (run-004/asset-three-quarter.png).
observations.silhouette_quality: The roof-dominated outline reads as a shed before a clockwork workshop; the twin panels leave little space for the defining machinery in run-004/settlement-scale.png.
observations.surface_variation: Board color courses and metal seams vary across the rendered surfaces, although the roof panels remain visually uniform.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 import/bounds checks pass; the run-004 receipt reports this exact candidate/path through the normal RoomScale resolver with production_path=true.
